groups.@pages: heading in the @ menu (links to anything in the workspace) over the pages it found
groups.@assignments: heading in the @ menu over the assignments (homework) it found
groups.@events: heading in the @ menu over the calendar events it found
groups.@files: heading in the @ menu over the files it found
groups.@create: heading in the @ menu over the entries that make a new page or assignment named after what was typed (a verb)

mention.@eventRepeats: under a repeating calendar event in the @ menu; {date} is its first date, like Oct 14
mention.@newPage: @ menu entry that makes a new page and links to it; {query} is what was typed after the @, which becomes the page's title
mention.@newPageHint: under “New page …” in the @ menu: the new page goes inside the page being written in
mention.@newAssignment: @ menu entry that makes a new assignment and links to it; {query} is what was typed after the @, which becomes its title
mention.@newAssignmentHint: under “New assignment …” in the @ menu; Assignments is the name of the view that lists them
mention.@nothingFound: shown in the @ menu when nothing matches what was typed

notHere.@page: shown in place of a link to a page that isn't in this workspace (someone else's page, in a page written together, or one deleted for good)
notHere.@assignment: shown in place of a link to an assignment that isn't in this workspace (someone else's, or deleted for good)
notHere.@event: shown in place of a link to a calendar event that isn't in this workspace (someone else's, or deleted for good)
notHere.@file: shown in place of a link to a file that isn't in this workspace (someone else's, or deleted for good)

deleted.@page: shown in place of a link to a page that is in the Trash
deleted.@assignment: shown in place of a link to an assignment that is in the Trash
deleted.@event: shown in place of a link to a calendar event that is in the Trash
deleted.@file: shown in place of a link to a file that is in the Trash

chip.@markDone: label of the round checkbox on an assignment linked in a page, when the assignment isn't done
chip.@markNotDone: label of the round checkbox on an assignment linked in a page, when the assignment is done

file.@fallbackName: the name shown for a file linked in a page when it has no name or can't be found (a noun)
file.@missing: on a file's card in a page, in place of its size, when the file itself is gone from the computer (it was moved or deleted outside the app)
file.@openInDefaultApp: tooltip of the button on a file's card that opens the file in the program the computer opens that kind of file with
file.@deleted: title of a file's card in a page when the file was deleted
file.@restoreFromTrash: under “Deleted file” on a file's card; the Trash is where deleted things go

meeting.@defaultTitle: the title a new meeting block starts with (the block that records and transcribes a meeting); {date} is the date and time it was added, like Nov 16, 2:30 PM
meeting.@titleLabel: accessible name and placeholder of the text field holding a meeting block's title
meeting.@record: button on a meeting block that starts recording the meeting (a verb)
meeting.@stop: button on a meeting block that ends the recording and starts making the transcript (a verb)
meeting.@pause: button on a meeting block that pauses the recording (a verb)
meeting.@resume: button on a meeting block that carries on a paused recording (a verb)

sources.label: Record from
sources.@label: accessible name of the two switches on a meeting block that choose what is recorded: the microphone and the sound the Mac plays
sources.@mic: switch on a meeting block: record the microphone (short for microphone)
sources.@system: switch on a meeting block: record the sound the Mac itself is playing, such as the other people on a video call
sources.@micLevel: accessible name of the level meter showing how loud the microphone is while recording
sources.@systemLevel: accessible name of the level meter showing how loud the Mac's own sound is while recording

meeting.@recording: shown on a meeting block while it records (a status, not a button)
meeting.@paused: shown on a meeting block while its recording is paused (a status)

stage.@transcribing: shown on a meeting block while the speech is being turned into text; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100
stage.@saving: shown on a meeting block while the finished recording and transcript are being stored (one word, with an ellipsis)
stage.@reidentifying: shown on a meeting block while the speakers are being found again; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100

meeting.@cancel: button on a meeting block that stops making the transcript
meeting.@failed: title shown on a meeting block when making the transcript failed; the reason follows
meeting.@retry: button on a meeting block that tries making the transcript again (a verb)
meeting.interrupted: This recording was saved but doesn't have a transcript yet.
meeting.interruptedHint: ThoughtNotes was closed before it finished.
meeting.@process: button on a meeting block that turns a saved recording into a transcript (a verb)
meeting.@discard: button on a meeting block that throws away a recording that wasn't turned into a transcript
meeting.empty: No speech was found in this recording.
meeting.@player: accessible name of the audio player on a meeting block
meeting.@speakers: accessible name of the row of speaker names above a meeting's transcript (the people who spoke)
meeting.@me: the name of the person using the app, as a speaker in a meeting transcript (the other speakers are Speaker 1, Speaker 2, …)
meeting.speaker: Speaker {number}
meeting.@speaker: the name given to a person heard in a meeting recording; {number} is 1, 2, 3 in the order they first spoke
meeting.@renameSpeaker: tooltip of a speaker's name above a meeting transcript, which can be clicked to give them a name; {name} is the name now
meeting.@speakerName: accessible name of the text field for typing a speaker's new name
meeting.@seek: tooltip of a time in a meeting transcript; clicking it plays the recording from there; {time} is like 1:05
meeting.@copy: button on a meeting block that copies the whole transcript as plain text
meeting.@copied: message shown after the meeting transcript was copied
meeting.@rerun: button on a meeting block that works out again who said what
meeting.@rerunCount: label of the field next to Re-run speaker detection where the number of people can be entered
meeting.@rerunAuto: placeholder of the number-of-people field: ThoughtNotes works the number out itself
meeting.@rerunGo: button that starts working out who said what again (a verb)
meeting.@delete: button on a meeting block that removes the audio and the transcript, leaving an empty meeting
meeting.deleteConfirmMessage: The audio and the transcript are removed from this page. This can't be undone.
meeting.@deleteConfirm: button that confirms deleting a meeting's recording and transcript (a verb)
meeting.audioMissing: The recording's audio file is gone, but the transcript is still here.

notice.screenDenied: System audio is off because Screen Recording isn't allowed for ThoughtNotes. Only the microphone is being recorded. Allow it in System Settings, then restart ThoughtNotes.
notice.systemFailed: System audio couldn't start ({reason}). Only the microphone is being recorded.
notice.@systemFailed: notice on a meeting block; {reason} is the system's explanation
notice.@micFailed: notice on a meeting block; {reason} is the system's explanation
notice.micSilent: The microphone isn't picking up any sound. Check that ThoughtNotes is allowed to use it in System Settings.

models.title: Download the speech models
models.body: To make transcripts, ThoughtNotes needs speech models. They are downloaded once, from the model publishers, and then everything runs on this Mac. Your audio and text never leave it.
models.@speechModel: row in the model download sheet; {name} is the chosen quality, such as Best
models.@total: under the list of models to download; {size} is a size like 620.5 MB
models.@download: button that starts downloading the speech models (a verb)
models.@downloading: shown while the models download; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100
models.@unpacking: shown in the model download sheet while a downloaded file is being unpacked (one word, with an ellipsis)
models.@failed: shown when the model download fails; {reason} is the explanation
models.@retry: button that starts the model download again
models.@summaryTitle: title of the sheet that explains the download of the model that writes meeting summaries
models.summaryBody: To write meeting summaries, ThoughtNotes needs a language model. It's downloaded once, from the model's publisher, and then runs on this Mac. Your transcripts never leave it.
models.@summaryBody: explains the summary model download before it starts
models.@summaryModel: the one item in the summary model download list; Qwen3.5 4B is the model's name, keep it as is

meeting.@summaryHeading: the heading put above a meeting's summary when the page is exported to Markdown or Word (the summary is the short write-up of the meeting made from its transcript)

general.name: General
general.@name: name of the default meeting type (a meeting type tells the app how to write a meeting's summary), for any kind of meeting
general.instructions:
Write these sections:
## Overview: two or three sentences on what the meeting was about.
## Decisions: what was decided.
## Action items: each task, with its owner in bold when one was named.
## Notes by speaker: the main points each person made.
general.@instructions: the default instructions of the General meeting type, editable in Settings. This text is sent as instructions to the summarizing model, which runs on this Mac; translate it naturally and keep the section names short.

oneOnOne.@name: name of the meeting type for a one-on-one meeting between two people, usually a manager and someone on their team (keep it short)
oneOnOne.instructions:
This is a one-on-one between two people. Write these sections:
## Overview: what was discussed, in two or three sentences.
## Feedback: feedback given or asked for, by whom.
## Blockers and support needed: what's in the way and what help was asked for.
## Follow-ups: what each person will do next, with the owner in bold.
oneOnOne.@instructions: the default instructions of the 1:1 meeting type. This text is sent as instructions to the summarizing model, which runs on this Mac; translate it naturally and keep the section names short.

team.name: Team meeting
team.@name: name of the meeting type for a regular meeting of a team
team.instructions:
This is a team meeting. Write these sections:
## Overview: what the meeting covered.
## Updates by person: each person's update, under their name in bold.
## Decisions: what the team decided.
## Action items: each task, with its owner in bold.
## Open questions: what was left unresolved.
team.@instructions: the default instructions of the Team meeting type. This text is sent as instructions to the summarizing model, which runs on this Mac; translate it naturally and keep the section names short.

sales.name: Sales call
sales.@name: name of the meeting type for a call with a customer or prospective customer
sales.instructions:
This is a sales call with a customer. Write these sections:
## Overview: who the customer is and what the call was about.
## Customer needs: their goals and pain points, in their words where possible.
## Objections: concerns they raised and how they were answered.
## Pricing and timeline: any prices, budgets or dates mentioned.
## Next steps: what happens next, with owners in bold.
sales.@instructions: the default instructions of the Sales call meeting type. This text is sent as instructions to the summarizing model, which runs on this Mac; translate it naturally and keep the section names short.

tabs.label: Meeting views
tabs.@label: accessible name of the row of tabs on a meeting block (the tabs switch between the meeting's summary and its transcript)
tabs.@summary: tab on a meeting block that shows the short write-up of the meeting made from its transcript
tabs.@transcript: tab on a meeting block that shows the full transcript: who said what, with times

summary.@type: label of the menu on a meeting's Summary tab that picks the meeting type (1:1, Team meeting, Sales call…), which tells the app how to write the summary
summary.@editTypes: last item of the meeting type menu; opens Settings › Meetings where meeting types are edited
summary.@summarize: button on a meeting's Summary tab that writes the summary from the transcript, on this Mac
summary.@regenerate: button on a meeting's Summary tab that writes the summary again (for example after the meeting type changed)
summary.@cancel: button that stops a meeting summary that is being written
summary.@copy: button that copies a meeting's summary to the clipboard
summary.@copied: short confirmation shown after a meeting's summary was copied to the clipboard
summary.@writing: status shown while the summary of a meeting is being written on this Mac
summary.waiting: Waiting for another summary or recording to finish…
summary.@waiting: status shown while a meeting's summary waits its turn: only one summary is written at a time, and not while a recording is being turned into a transcript
summary.@failed: heading shown when writing a meeting's summary failed; the reason follows it
summary.@retry: button that tries writing a meeting's summary again after it failed
summary.stale: Written as {type}. Regenerate to use the current type.
summary.@stale: hint shown when the meeting type or its instructions changed since the summary was written; {type} is the meeting type that wrote it, like Team meeting
summary.@footer: small line under a meeting's summary; {type} is the meeting type that wrote it (like 1:1), {time} the date and time, like Nov 17, 3:05 PM
summary.@noModel: heading on a meeting's Summary tab when the model that writes summaries hasn't been downloaded
summary.noModelHint: It runs on this Mac, so your meetings never leave it. It's a one-time download of {size}.
summary.@noModelHint: explains the summary model download; {size} is its size, like 2.7 GB
summary.@download: button that starts downloading the model that writes meeting summaries
summary.@none: shown on a meeting's Summary tab before a summary was written

database.@fallbackTitle: the name used for a database shown in a page when it has no title (a noun)

callout.@changeIcon: tooltip of the icon at the start of a callout box: click to pick another icon or emoji

flashcard.@front: small heading over a flashcard's first side (the term or question)
flashcard.@back: small heading over a flashcard's second side (the definition or answer)

images.@tooLarge: message when an image added to a page is too big; {size} is the largest size allowed, with its unit, like 25 MB

math.@emptyBlock: shown in an equation block (a formula on its own line) that is still empty; click to write it
math.@emptyInline: shown in a formula inside a line of text that is still empty; click to write it
math.@field: accessible name of the box where a formula's LaTeX source is typed
math.@placeholder: placeholder in the box where a formula's LaTeX is typed; {example} is a sample formula (E = mc^2 or x^2); \ is the backslash key, which opens the list of LaTeX commands. Keep the spaces after {example}
math.@commands: accessible name of the list of LaTeX commands suggested while typing after a backslash
math.@symbols: button under the formula box that shows or hides a palette of math symbols to click
math.@hintBlock: keyboard hint under the box for an equation on its own line: Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) finishes, Tab goes to the next empty {} box of the formula; {mod} is the Ctrl key's name (⌘ on a Mac). Inside <kbd> are key names as keyboards in your language label them
math.@hintInline: keyboard hint under the box for a formula inside a line of text: Enter finishes, Tab goes to the next empty {} box of the formula. Inside <kbd> are key names as keyboards in your language label them

palette.@structures: tab of the math symbol palette: fractions, roots, sums, integrals, matrices
palette.@greek: tab of the math symbol palette: Greek letters (α, β, Γ)
palette.@operators: tab of the math symbol palette: ±, ×, ∂, ∞, ∪ and the like
palette.@relations: tab of the math symbol palette: ≠, ≤, ≈, ∈, ⊂ and the like
palette.@arrows: tab of the math symbol palette: →, ⇒, ↔ and the like

math.@casesIf: written into a formula when someone inserts a piecewise definition (\begin{cases}): “value if condition”. Plain words only: no { } \ | $ & # ^ _ % or ~
math.@casesOtherwise: written into a formula when someone inserts a piecewise definition (\begin{cases}), as the last case's condition. Plain words only: no { } \ | $ & # ^ _ % or ~
math.@search: Words that find a LaTeX command when typed after a backslash in a formula (\fract… finds \frac), never shown. Space-separated, lower case. Only the letters a–z can be typed after the backslash, so write words without accents where your language allows; the English words keep working too

search.@int: search word for \int, the integral sign (see the note on this group)
search.@lim: search word for \lim, a limit (see the note on this group)
search.@dv: search word for a derivative dy/dx (see the note on this group)
search.@pmatrix: search word for a matrix in round brackets (see the note on this group)
search.@vmatrix: search word for a determinant, a matrix between bars (see the note on this group)
search.@cases: search word for a piecewise definition, cases one under another (see the note on this group)
search.@operators: search word for operator symbols like ±, ×, ⊕ (see the note on this group)
search.@symbols: search word for symbols like ∂, ∇, ∞, ℏ (see the note on this group)
search.@relations: search word for relations like ≠, ≤, ≈, ≡ (see the note on this group)
search.@arrows: search word for arrows like →, ⇒, ↔ (see the note on this group)
search.@functions: search word for function names written upright, like sin, log, max (see the note on this group)
search.@brackets: search word for \left( … \right), brackets that grow with what they hold (see the note on this group)
search.@overrightarrow: search word for an arrow over a vector's name, like AB with → over it (see the note on this group)
search.@mathcal: search word for calligraphic letters, like ℒ (see the note on this group)
